evidence.observation: "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population."
No CG1 acceptance case covers a second document's rows that violate a uniqueness, mandatory or value constraint satisfied by the first document's rows; the only CG-specific cases are for CG2 and CG3.

concerns.recommendation: State the outcome when the extended population fails validation: refuse the whole batch, which constraint and which rows are reported, and whether the preview shows the conflict before CAS. Add an acceptance pair: document A rows valid, document B adds a row conflicting on a uniqueness constraint, apply refused with the model bytes unchanged; and the same case without the conflict accepted.
concerns.title: CG1 does not define behavior when appended rows conflict with existing constraints

evidence.observation: "Preview row moves and role rewrites together, record merge, demotion, subtype or leave, recompute candidates after apply"
"After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row's original source." Only the successful path is checked; there is no failure or CAS-conflict case.

concerns.recommendation: Require that the row moves, role-reference rewrites and decision-log entry are published in one CAS, or none of them are. Add a falsifiable case: a stale CAS or a validation failure partway through the rewrite leaves the model, the population and the decision log unchanged, and no decision is recorded as applied.
concerns.title: Row/role rewrites are previewed together, but nothing requires the apply to be atomic

evidence.observation: "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold."
"Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." No limits are named.

concerns.recommendation: Say what the threshold measures (candidate score floor, number of remaining groups, rounds, or reviewed groups). Add a hard round cap so the loop cannot run forever when a merge creates new similarity candidates. Add a case where a merge produces a new candidate group and the loop still stops at the cap, recording the counter and the stop reason.
concerns.title: Loop termination is defined only as 'the configured threshold', with no metric or round bound

evidence.observation: "shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans. Include two similarly named types with incompatible role players; the suggestion must carry evidence for review."
"Index singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns."

concerns.recommendation: Add a recall fixture: at least one planted duplicate per listed signal (singleton type, role-player shape, reading shape, name similarity, unit, counted noun) must each be grouped. Take the #339 reproduction's known duplicate set and assert it is found. Also add a negative case per signal that must not be grouped.
concerns.title: No criterion checks that candidate discovery finds the duplicates it claims to index

evidence.observation: "Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows."

concerns.recommendation: Define when two rows are the same row (exact tuple equality, or equality after normalization) and what a repeat does: attach an extra span to the existing row, refuse it, or no-op. Add cases for: the same row from the same span applied twice (idempotent), the same row from a different document (one row, two spans), and a near-duplicate that differs only by normalization.
concerns.title: Duplicate observations are counted but row identity and the attach/refuse rule are undefined

evidence.observation: "Append located rows to a locally owned fact"
"State validation order at each public boundary and test both sides of every refusal." The plan states no order for CG1 and names no ownership refusal.

concerns.recommendation: Define 'locally owned' (declared in this model, not imported or derived). Name the refusal for appending to a non-owned fact and state the CG1 validation order, e.g. ownership → span-in-document → population constraints → CAS. Test both sides of the ownership refusal.
concerns.title: 'Locally owned fact' and the CG1 validation order are not defined

evidence.observation: "Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338. The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract and requires revising CG1."
"CG1 provides the canonical evidence representation for CG2 and CG3."

concerns.recommendation: Settle D1 before this plan is approved, or write CG1, CG2 and CG3 exit criteria for both storage options. The evidence representation, the CAS scope and CG3's atomic rewrite all depend on the choice.
concerns.title: The unresolved storage choice undermines the CG1 criterion and CG2/CG3's evidence dependency

evidence.observation: "After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row's original source."

concerns.recommendation: Add a case where merging two types moves rows that collide with the target's rows or break a uniqueness constraint after the move. Specify whether the merge is refused or the rows are deduplicated with both provenances kept.
concerns.title: Merging can produce duplicate or constraint-violating rows, and no case covers it

evidence.observation: "Emit stable candidate IDs"
"Vary identifiers, declaration order and input cardinality in the acceptance fixtures."

concerns.recommendation: Say what candidate IDs are derived from and which changes they must survive: declaration reordering, recomputation after an unrelated merge, and renaming a type that is not a group member. If IDs are derived from names, they change exactly when the fixtures vary identifiers.
concerns.title: The basis for stable candidate IDs is unspecified and may conflict with varying identifiers

evidence.observation: "accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes."
"record merge, demotion, subtype or leave". 'decline' is not one of the recorded decisions.

concerns.recommendation: Align the vocabulary (decline vs leave). Define 'evidence changes' as a digest over member types, role players and cited spans. Bind each log entry to the model revision it was made against. Add the positive case: changed evidence re-offers the group.
concerns.title: Decision-log suppression rule and its vocabulary are underspecified

evidence.observation: "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply."
"name similarity". Pairwise comparison over all types, with no stated limit.

concerns.recommendation: Name the work limits (types indexed, pairwise comparisons, groups emitted, rows moved per apply). Name the counter recorded for each and the refusal when a limit is exceeded. Add a cardinality fixture that crosses each limit.
concerns.title: No work limits are named for discovery or apply

evidence.observation: "the closure replay must exercise two documents and an accepted merge."
"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases"

concerns.recommendation: State what the replay compares: a byte-identical model and population after re-running the decision log on the same inputs, the same candidate IDs, and every row's span still resolving to its document. Include a declined group and a duplicate observation in the replay.
concerns.title: The replay does not say what it compares or that it is deterministic

evidence.observation: "Growth policy currently directs later rows to open questions. Changing that public guidance belongs to CG1."

concerns.recommendation: Say whether appending is opt-in or becomes the default. If it becomes the default, pin the old open-questions behavior for callers who have not opted in, as §9's "pin the old behavior on unextended inputs" suggests.
concerns.title: Unclear whether later-row appends replace the open-questions default

response.summary: The plan names the right areas for #338 and #339, but the exit criteria are not yet falsifiable on the points the rubric stresses. For #338 it leaves open how appends that conflict with existing constraints are handled, how a row's identity is decided when the same observation repeats, and what makes a fact locally owned. For #339 it does not define the termination threshold or any work bound, does not say apply is atomic, does not test recall, and leaves stable IDs, decision-log binding and replay comparison undefined. Unresolved storage decision D1 also undermines the CG1 criterion and the evidence representation CG2 and CG3 depend on.

evidence.observation: "Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows." The referenced CG1 draft spec also says identical rows from distinct documents need an explicit provenance ruling, but the plan supplies no expected result.

concerns.recommendation: Specify how one tuple supported by two documents is stored, counted, previewed and replayed; test repeated observations from both the same and different documents.
concerns.title: Duplicate rows lack a provenance contract

evidence.observation: "Preview row moves and role rewrites together" specifies a combined preview but does not require an atomic apply or rollback if either rewrite fails.

concerns.recommendation: Require one atomic publication of row moves and role rewrites, and verify that an injected failure between them leaves the model unchanged.
concerns.title: Combined rewrites are not required to publish atomically

evidence.observation: "restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes" checks declined decisions only. It does not define replay behavior for an accepted merge.

concerns.recommendation: Bind accepted decisions to their input state and test restart after an applied merge, including repeated replay and changed source evidence, without duplicate rows or repeated rewrites.
concerns.title: Accepted merges have no replay contract

evidence.observation: The exit criterion says "Index singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns." The specified fixtures only "shuffle model declaration order" and include "two similarly named types with incompatible role players"; they do not require a candidate for each listed cue.

concerns.recommendation: Add positive, differently named witness cases for each discovery cue and assert the complete expected candidate set and evidence locations.
concerns.title: Discovery tests do not establish candidate completeness

evidence.observation: The loop will "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold," while §6 asks to "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." Neither passage sets a discovery work limit or a no-progress termination rule.

concerns.recommendation: Define budgets for candidate generation and loop iterations, plus a no-progress stop; test a large dense candidate set and a decision that leaves the model unchanged.
concerns.title: Candidate generation and the review loop lack enforceable bounds

evidence.observation: CG1 permits additions to a "locally owned fact" and requires validation of the extended population. The verification instruction uses the issue reproduction and §4 criterion, without a case that attempts to change a source-owned fact or introduces a conflicting constraint from a second document.

concerns.recommendation: Specify the refusal and unchanged-state result for additions to a nonlocal fact and for a second document whose constraint conflicts with the existing model; include both in CG1 acceptance.
concerns.title: Ownership and conflicting-constraint refusals are not demonstrated

response.summary: The plan covers the intended phases but leaves several safety and acceptance contracts unresolved.

evidence.observation: "Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338. The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract and requires revising CG1."

"For each later phase, use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair" — §9 then gives explicit fixtures only for "CG2:" and "CG3:"; CG1 gets only "Run the first spec’s focused selection and retain its verbatim pytest summary."

concerns.recommendation: Either decide the storage question in this plan or restate CG1 so its §4 exit criterion holds under both options, and add a plan-level CG1 acceptance pair (issue 338 reproduction plus the §4 criterion) covering the additive preview/apply sequence, the intact-prior-rows assertion and one population-validation refusal, instead of delegating all of it to phase-CG1-spec.md.
concerns.title: CG1's own §10 decision can invalidate CG1, and CG1 is the only phase with no acceptance case in §9

evidence.location: §0 Binding design rules and §2 Proposed behavior (CG1)
evidence.observation: The only validation language is "Document and check every new sample span against the cited document before CAS." and "Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population." The words conflict, contradiction or incompatible constraint appear nowhere for appended rows; §2 CG2 mentions "incompatible role players" only as a candidate-discovery signal.

"Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population." — no disposition is stated for a new located row that contradicts an existing row, unit or role-player constraint.

concerns.recommendation: Define conflict detection and disposition for appended rows (refuse the apply, quarantine to open questions, or record both with provenance and a recorded winner), state which side prevails and at which boundary the check runs, and add a falsifiable fixture that appends a row contradicting an existing constraint, testing both sides of the refusal as §0 requires.
concerns.title: Issue 338 conflicting constraints have no rule, no winner and no fixture

evidence.observation: "CG1 provides the canonical evidence representation for CG2 and CG3." No field-level contract follows anywhere in the plan: source document identity, span offsets, span or document digest, per-row origin and observation-versus-row distinction are never enumerated.

"Append located rows to a locally owned fact" — "locally owned" is used as the only ownership predicate and is never defined, so the ownership check that §0 places "before CAS" has no stated subject or refusal.

concerns.recommendation: Add a field-level contract for the evidence record (owning fact, source document identity, span range, span digest, origin row identity, duplicate count) and an explicit ownership predicate with its refusal, name the component that owns it from the §3 list, and require CG2 and CG3 specs to consume only that contract so the dependency in §3 is checkable.
concerns.title: CG1 is declared the canonical evidence representation for CG2/CG3 but its contents and the ownership predicate are never defined

evidence.observation: "Review one group at a time against source spans. Preview row moves and role rewrites together, record merge, demotion, subtype or leave, recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold." The threshold's quantity and configuration key are never named (rounds, accepted merges, remaining candidate count, or a score floor).

The CG3 cases are "accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log" and post-rename validation; no case exercises the stopping condition or a recompute that regenerates an already-reviewed candidate.

concerns.recommendation: Name the bounded quantity, its configuration key and default; state the progress invariant that makes recompute terminate (each apply strictly reduces the candidate set or consumes a round counter); and add a fixture in which an accepted merge regenerates the same candidate group, asserting the loop stops at the threshold and records the counter.
concerns.title: Loop termination rests on an unnamed "configured threshold" with no progress invariant and no fixture

evidence.observation: "Preview row moves and role rewrites together, record merge, demotion, subtype or leave" — togetherness is required of the preview, but no all-or-nothing rule, rollback behaviour or partial-failure disposition is stated for the apply.

"The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract" presupposes an atomic publication and summary contract for the in-model option, but neither contract is defined anywhere in the plan; §0 mentions CAS only for sample spans.

concerns.recommendation: State the atomic unit explicitly (one reviewed group apply is a single CAS over moved rows, rewritten role references and the summary), the behaviour when one role rewrite fails validation mid-apply, and the validation order; add a fixture with one invalid role rewrite asserting that no row moved and that the refusal is the first recorded one.
concerns.title: Atomic row and role rewrites are referenced as a contract in §10 but never defined for CG3 apply

evidence.observation: "Emit stable candidate IDs, evidence locations and scores. Reordering declarations must preserve groups." Stability is bound only to declaration reordering.

CG2 tests "shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans"; CG3 requires "restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes" after another group was accepted, but nothing requires IDs of untouched groups to survive the intervening "recompute candidates after apply".

concerns.recommendation: Require candidate and group IDs to be content-derived and stable across CG3 recompute for groups whose evidence is unchanged, and extend the §9 CG3 case to assert that the declined group's ID is byte-identical after an accepted merge elsewhere, so suppression in the decision log is keyed on a stable identifier.
concerns.title: Candidate ID stability is required against reordering but not across CG3 recompute, which the declined-group test depends on

evidence.observation: "verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes" — the plan defines no identity or version token for evidence (span digest, document digest, row set), so the exception clause cannot be evaluated.
"Document and check every new sample span against the cited document before CAS." establishes a span check but no persisted digest that a later recompute could compare against.

concerns.recommendation: Define evidence identity as a digest over the cited spans and rows, require it in the decision-log record, and add two fixtures: unchanged source (declined group suppressed) and edited source document (declined group re-offered with the new digest), each asserting the recorded comparison.
concerns.title: "unless its evidence changes" has no evidence identity, so the §9 declined-group assertion is not falsifiable

evidence.observation: Both sections repeat only "Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows." The plan never states what makes two observations duplicates (same span cited twice, same row reached from two documents, identical role-player triple), whether a duplicate is appended, merged or refused, or where the separate count is surfaced.
§9 lists CG2 and CG3 fixtures and a general "Vary identifiers, declaration order and input cardinality in the acceptance fixtures" (in §6), but no CG1 case appends the same evidence twice.

concerns.recommendation: Define the duplicate key and its disposition, require the apply summary to report duplicate versus distinct counts as separate fields, and add a CG1 fixture that appends the same span from two documents plus one that appends the same span twice from one document, asserting the counts and the population validation outcome.
concerns.title: Duplicate evidence is to be counted separately but duplicates are never identified, dispositioned or surfaced

evidence.observation: "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." No limit is defined anywhere in the plan: candidates per round, spans per document, rows per apply, group size, decision-log length or recompute rounds are all absent.

The CG3 exit criterion ends at "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold" and contains no bounded-work or counter requirement, so the §6 control has no observable exit criterion.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the limits with configuration keys and defaults, name the counter fields that must appear in the summary, add bounded work to the CG3 §4 exit criterion, and add a fixture that exceeds one limit and asserts both the recorded counter and the first refusal message.
concerns.title: Bounded work is a named control with no bound, no counter contract and no exit criterion

evidence.observation: "Index singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns." Five candidate classes are claimed as the deliverable.

"shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans. Include two similarly named types with incompatible role players" exercises name similarity and role-player shape only; singleton types, reading shapes, units and counted nouns have no fixture, and no CG2 case produces a candidate whose evidence spans two documents even though §3 requires the closure replay to "exercise two documents and an accepted merge".

concerns.recommendation: Add one acceptance fixture per candidate class plus a candidate whose evidence is drawn from two different documents, and state the completeness check explicitly (every indexed class yields at least one candidate group in the acceptance model, and no indexed class is silently empty).
concerns.title: CG2 claims five candidate classes but §9 fixtures cover two, and no phase-level case is cross-document

evidence.observation: "Candidate discovery may read a model before CG1 ships, but the closure replay must exercise two documents and an accepted merge." The replay's assertions, entry points and owning artifact are not stated.

"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims." — nothing says what the replay must show (deterministic candidate IDs, identical model and summary output, equivalence between a fresh run and a decision-log resumption).

concerns.recommendation: Define the closure replay as a named fixture with explicit assertions and recorded public entry points, and require it to run twice: once from a clean state and once resuming from a persisted decision log, asserting identical model, summary and candidate IDs.
concerns.title: The milestone-close replay is mandated twice but its assertions and artifact home are never defined

evidence.observation: "State validation order at each public boundary and test both sides of every refusal." The plan never lists the boundaries this applies to (additive preview, apply, candidate query, review decision, decision-log restart).
"record the public entry point and result" is required per phase, but with no boundary inventory the reviewer cannot tell whether the recorded entry points cover every refusal path.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the public entry points in §2 or §4 and require each phase spec to carry a validation-order table with one passing and one refusing case per entry point, so the both-sides rule in §0 is checkable at spec review.
concerns.title: The validation-order and both-sides-of-refusal rule has no list of boundaries to apply it to

evidence.observation: "Growth policy currently directs later rows to open questions. Changing that public guidance belongs to CG1." and "Run existing examples and compare the observable result for a caller using the previous interface." No example is named and no additive-versus-breaking statement is made.

CG1's criterion is only "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population." — the §5 documentation change and prior-interface comparison are absent from the table that §9 uses as the acceptance pair.

concerns.recommendation: Add the docs/reference/evolve-policy.md guidance change and a named existing example run with a recorded before/after result to CG1's §4 exit criterion, and state whether the public guidance change is additive or breaking for callers on the previous interface.
concerns.title: CG1 owns a public guidance change in §5 that §4's exit criterion does not track

evidence.observation: "The component index identifies `evolve.policy`, `evolve.population_check`, `evolve.service`, `evolve.round_summary`. Its November 27 review flagged 105 descriptions older than their source; resolve contract details against code and tests." The plan nonetheless assigns ownership of the new contracts to those components and names src/gnd/evolve/policy.py as the starting point.
"Implementation baseline 83cd4170." is pinned, but no step requires confirming at that baseline that the four named components still own the contracts §3 assigns to them.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit pre-implementation step in the CG1 spec that confirms each named component and its contract at baseline 83cd4170 against code and tests, and require any re-assignment of ownership to be recorded in the phase record rather than discovered during diff review.
concerns.title: Component ownership is taken from an index the plan itself reports as 105 descriptions stale

evidence.observation: "record merge, demotion, subtype or leave" names four actions but no record contents and no rule for a group whose members would receive different actions.
"restart from the decision log" is required, yet the plan never states what a restart does with a group that was partially reviewed when the process stopped.

concerns.recommendation: Specify the decision-record fields (group ID, evidence digest, chosen action per member, affected rows and roles, ordering, actor) and the mixed-action rule, and add a fixture that interrupts mid-group and asserts the group is re-offered whole rather than partially applied on restart.
concerns.title: Review decision records and mixed-action or interrupted groups are undefined, weakening the restart guarantee

evidence.observation: "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply." No refusal is defined for a target fact that is not locally owned, or for a cited document outside the owned corpus.

"After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row" — origin recovery is required only as a post-hoc check, not as retained immutable data on the moved row, and no case combines a CG3 row move with a later rename and restart.

concerns.recommendation: Define the ownership predicate and its refusal at the apply boundary, require an immutable origin field (source document, span, prior fact) persisted on every moved row, and extend the §9 case to assert that origin survives move plus rename plus restart.
concerns.title: Source ownership has no refusal path and transferred-row provenance is checked but not required to be retained

response.summary: The plan is coherent, cites both issues and pins a baseline, but the safety properties the rubric names are stated as slogans rather than decided semantics. CG1 is the phase whose storage model §10 admits may require revising CG1, yet CG1 is also the only phase with no plan-level acceptance pair in §9. Conflicting constraints (issue 338) are never addressed, duplicate-evidence counting and source ownership have no identity rule or refusal, and for issue 339 the termination threshold, work bounds, atomic row/role apply, candidate-ID stability across recompute, the evidence-change predicate and the closure replay assertions are all undefined, so several §4 exit criteria are not falsifiable as written. Sixteen concerns follow; revise before the owner ruling.

evidence.observation: Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply.
Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338. The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract and requires revising CG1.

concerns.recommendation: Resolve the open decision on storage location (in-model vs external) before approving the plan, as CG1 requires this decision to proceed and currently hardcodes a conflicting state.
concerns.title: Contradiction between CG1 definition and open decision for source ownership

evidence.observation: Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population.

concerns.recommendation: Explicitly define the failure mode, reporting mechanism, and resolution path for conflicting constraints (e.g., cardinality or type violations) when validating the extended population.
concerns.title: Missing resolution for conflicting constraints during append

evidence.observation: After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row’s original source.

concerns.recommendation: Add a falsifiable test case that intentionally interrupts or fails a role rewrite to verify that the operation rolls back atomically without partial state changes.
concerns.title: Missing falsifiable case for atomic rewrite failure

evidence.observation: recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold.
Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply.

concerns.recommendation: Specify the exact unit of the 'configured threshold' and limits (e.g., max loop iterations, processed candidates) to establish a clear, falsifiable limit for bounded work in the consolidation loop.
concerns.title: Ambiguous threshold unit for bounded work limit

response.summary: The plan establishes a clear phase structure but contains a blocking contradiction on source ownership and lacks necessary details for constraint conflicts and atomicity verification.

evidence.observation: §0 makes duplicate handling binding ("Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows.") and §2/§4 promise appends to "a locally owned fact", but the CG1 observable exit criterion is only "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population." and §9 defines acceptance as "the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair". No criterion or §9 verification entry exercises a duplicate observation (same row from two documents), a conflicting constraint between the new row and the existing population, or an ownership refusal (append to a fact the local model does not own), so the milestone can close without demonstrating the very behaviors §0 binds.

concerns.recommendation: Add explicit CG1 acceptance cases to §4/§9: identical row arriving from two distinct documents (counted as duplicate evidence, not two rows), a new row violating an existing constraint (refusal with stated order), and an append attempted against a non-locally-owned fact (refusal).
concerns.title: CG1 exit criterion omits the duplicate-evidence, conflict and ownership behavior §0 makes binding

evidence.observation: §2 says "Preview row moves and role rewrites together" but nowhere states that apply is atomic or what happens when the row move validates and the role rewrite refuses. The repository's existing evolution machinery declares transaction_scope "single-leaf CAS; no multi-file atomicity" (src/gnd/evolve/models.py:1291), so a combined row/role consolidation plausibly spans leaves; the plan names no mechanism and §9's CG3 verification ("accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log...") contains no partial-failure or rollback case. §10 mentions "the atomic publication and summary contract" only for the external-population option, leaving the in-model path's atomicity unaddressed.

concerns.recommendation: State the apply atomicity contract for CG3 (single atomic publication or explicit compensation/rollback on mid-apply refusal) and add a §9 case that forces a role-rewrite refusal after a row move and asserts the model is byte-identical to its pre-apply state.
concerns.title: Atomicity of combined row-move/role-rewrite apply is unspecified and untested

evidence.observation: CG3's only termination semantics are "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold" — the threshold's quantity (score, group count, rounds), its configuration site, and the group review ordering are never defined. Because each apply recomputes candidates, a merge can generate new candidates indefinitely; no maximum-rounds, no-progress, or work budget is stated. §6 offers only "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply", which measures work without bounding it, and §9's CG3 cases cover accept/decline/restart but never that the loop actually terminates when declines dominate or when applies keep producing candidates.

concerns.recommendation: Define the threshold (what it counts, where configured, review order), state a hard bound (max rounds or max reviewed groups per run), and add a §9 case asserting termination with the recorded counters when candidate regeneration would otherwise continue.
concerns.title: CG3 loop termination and bounded work are claimed but not defined or testable

evidence.observation: CG2's criterion lists five signal classes ("singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns") and §9 verifies only order stability ("shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans") and evidence-carrying for one confusable pair. Nothing demonstrates recall: no fixture plants a known candidate per signal class (e.g., a unit mismatch or a counted-noun conflict) and asserts it is emitted, so "Index ... units and counted nouns" is not a demonstrable claim and a signal that silently produces nothing would pass every stated check.

concerns.recommendation: Add a per-signal seeded-candidate acceptance case: for each listed signal class, a fixture containing a known instance that must appear in the emitted candidates with its evidence location and score.
concerns.title: CG2 candidate completeness has no per-signal recall criterion

evidence.observation: §2/§4 write the CG1 behavior as decided — "Append located rows to a locally owned fact" — while §10 records "Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338" as open and warns the external option "requires revising CG1". The plan thus presents milestone completion criteria that are explicitly provisional, and since #338 is described as requesting the external population, the proposed in-model behavior deviates from the issue without a recorded rationale; a reader approving §4 approves a criterion the plan itself says may be voided by D1.

concerns.recommendation: Either record the rationale for proposing in-model append against #338's requested external population, or mark the CG1 row of §4 conditional on D1 and add the external-population variant's exit criterion so both resolution outcomes have completion criteria.
concerns.title: CG1 exit criterion prejudges the open D1 storage decision and deviates from #338's requested option without rationale

evidence.observation: §2 names four review decisions — "record merge, demotion, subtype or leave" — but never defines what demotion or subtype do to the model, and §9 tests only the accept/decline pair, leaving two of the four decision kinds without any observable outcome. The decision log that "restart from the decision log" and declined-group suppression depend on has no artifact home in §3 (which names only src/gnd/evolve/policy.py and components), and the suppression key is unspecified: §2 requires "stable candidate IDs" and "recompute candidates after apply", but whether a declined group is recognized by candidate ID or by evidence identity after recomputation is unstated, so the §9 guarantee "not offered again unless its evidence changes" has no defined mechanism.

concerns.recommendation: Define each decision kind's model effect, name the decision log's home and identity key (candidate ID vs evidence hash) in §3, and extend §9 with a demotion and a subtype case plus a recompute-after-apply case showing a declined group stays suppressed under regenerated IDs.
concerns.title: Review-decision vocabulary, decision-log home and suppression keying are undefined

evidence.observation: §3 states "CG1 provides the canonical evidence representation for CG2 and CG3. Candidate discovery may read a model before CG1 ships, but the closure replay must exercise two documents and an accepted merge." Because D1 (§10) can still replace in-model evidence with an external population, CG2 indexing built before CG1 ships may target an evidence representation that is then revised, and the only checkpoint is the closure replay — which is also scoped to just "two documents and an accepted merge", exercising neither a declined group nor a role rewrite.

concerns.recommendation: Either gate CG2 implementation on D1's resolution, or state explicitly which evidence-representation assumptions CG2 may rely on pre-CG1; widen the closure replay to include a declined group and a role rewrite so the replay covers the decision-log and atomicity paths.
concerns.title: CG2 may start against an evidence representation that D1 can still invalidate, and the closure replay is narrowly scoped

evidence.observation: §6 repeats §0's first two sentences verbatim: "Document and check every new sample span against the cited document before CAS. Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows." Duplicated normative text in two sections invites divergence when one copy is later revised (e.g., after D1 resolves), leaving the binding rule and the risk control stating different things.

concerns.recommendation: Keep the normative statement once in §0 and have §6 reference it, adding only the genuinely risk-specific controls (fixture variation, work counters) in §6.
concerns.title: §6 restates §0's binding rules verbatim, risking divergent copies

response.summary: Plan r1 for cross-document growth is coherent and honest about its open decision, but its acceptance machinery does not demonstrate several behaviors the rubric and the plan's own binding rules name: duplicate-observation/provenance-conflict handling for #338 has no falsifiable case, CG3 row/role rewrite atomicity and loop termination are unspecified against a codebase whose CAS is explicitly single-leaf, CG2 candidate completeness has no recall test, and the CG1 exit criterion prejudges the still-open D1 storage decision.

evidence.observation: Both state 'recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold', but no threshold is named or defined anywhere in the plan: it does not say what quantity is bounded (candidate score, review rounds, or work units), its default, or its configuration surface. A grep of src/gnd/evolve/ — the component set named in §3 line 23 — finds zero occurrences of 'threshold', so no existing configuration is being referenced either.

§6 only says generically 'Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply', and the CG3 acceptance cases in §9 are 'accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes' — decision persistence only; no case exercises the loop halting or a limit refusal.

concerns.recommendation: In the CG3 spec, name the threshold's quantity, default and configuration key, and add a §9 falsifiable case in which recompute keeps yielding eligible groups (for example a chain of similar types where each accepted merge exposes a new candidate) and assert the loop stops at the bound with the first refusal recorded.
concerns.title: Consolidation loop termination rests on an undefined 'configured threshold' and no acceptance case exercises halting

evidence.observation: 'Preview row moves and role rewrites together' binds only the preview; neither section states that apply performs the row moves and the role rewrites as one atomic, digest-bound unit, nor what is observable when one half is refused after the other has been staged. CG1 in contrast binds apply explicitly at §0 line 7: 'Document and check every new sample span against the cited document before CAS.'

The only related check is post-hoc and covers different operations: 'After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row's original source.' No case asserts an unchanged model when one half of a consolidation apply is refused.

concerns.recommendation: State in §2/§4 that a consolidation apply is a single CAS covering rows and roles together and that any refusal leaves the model byte-identical (mirroring the CG1 stale-preview rule in the spec), and add a §9 case in which the role rewrite is refused after the row moves are staged, asserting the model is unchanged.
concerns.title: Atomic apply of row moves with role rewrites is specified only at preview, not at apply

evidence.observation: 'Append located rows to a locally owned fact' uses ownership only as an eligibility adjective; the plan never states the observable behaviour when the target fact is not locally owned, which public boundary checks it, or where it sits in the validation order.

§0 demands 'State validation order at each public boundary and test both sides of every refusal', but no §9 CG1 case exercises a non-owned target; the referenced phase-CG1-spec.md §8 likewise tests only 'a fact introduced by A' plus citation and uniqueness refusals, so the ownership refusal is untested at both levels.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the ownership refusal (issue text, exit code, checking boundary) in §2/§4 and add a §9 fixture that locates rows onto an imported or externally owned fact and asserts publication is refused with the model byte-identical.
concerns.title: Source-ownership refusal path for a non-locally-owned target is unspecified and untested

evidence.observation: 'Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows' is asserted as a binding design rule in both sections.

'Keep prior rows and spans intact' permits a retried or repeated apply to append the same located rows twice; the plan states no idempotency rule for apply. Meanwhile §10 leaves storage open — 'Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338' — and the referenced phase-CG1-spec.md §6 says 'Identical rows with distinct supporting documents need an explicit provenance ruling' deferred under that open decision D1, so the binding counting rule presupposes an answer the plan itself marks unresolved.

concerns.recommendation: State whether apply is idempotent for repeated identical located rows, and either detach the identical-rows-from-distinct-documents ruling from the §10 storage decision or mark §0's counting rule conditional on it; add a §9 case that applies the same located rows twice and asserts the counted outcome.
concerns.title: Duplicate-observation counting is asserted as binding while identical-row provenance and apply idempotency are unresolved

evidence.observation: 'verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes' leaves 'evidence changes' undefined — no comparison (cited span set, document digest, candidate-defining inputs, score) is named, so the suppression exception is unfalsifiable as written and an implementation could re-offer any declined group after any unrelated model edit.

concerns.recommendation: Define the evidence-change comparison precisely in the CG3 spec (for example the group's cited span set or the inputs that define its candidate ID) and test both sides: re-offer after a genuine evidence change, no re-offer after an unrelated edit.
concerns.title: The replay suppression exception 'unless its evidence changes' has no defined comparison

evidence.observation: §4 states the CG1 observable exit criterion unconditionally — 'Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply' — while §10 makes that very behaviour an open owner choice: 'Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338. The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract and requires revising CG1.'

'use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair' makes the unconditional §4 text the acceptance anchor, so if the owner selects the external option the recorded acceptance pair tests the abandoned branch until §4 is revised.

concerns.recommendation: Mark the §4 CG1 criterion as conditional on the §10/D1 ruling, or fork it into one criterion per branch now, so the acceptance pair is valid under either owner decision.
concerns.title: The CG1 exit criterion commits to one branch of the open §10 storage decision

evidence.observation: 'Index singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns' enumerates six discovery dimensions.

The CG2 cases cover only ordering stability and name similarity: 'shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans. Include two similarly named types with incompatible role players; the suggestion must carry evidence for review.' No case asserts emission for the remaining dimensions, so dropping one (for example counted nouns) would fail no stated criterion.

concerns.recommendation: Map each indexed dimension to at least one emitting fixture in the CG2 spec (a small table of dimension, example, expected candidate), so the absence of any dimension is falsifiable.
concerns.title: No per-dimension coverage check ties the six indexed candidate dimensions to acceptance cases

response.summary: Digest verified. The r1 plan binds CG1-CG3 to the issue requirements with mostly falsifiable acceptance cases, and the referenced phase-CG1-spec.md supplies prefix/CAS ordering plus citation and uniqueness refusal cases. Two issue-339 aspects are not demonstrable as written: the consolidation loop's stopping condition rests on an undefined 'configured threshold' with no acceptance case exercising halting, and atomic apply of row moves together with role rewrites is specified only at preview. Ownership refusal, duplicate-append semantics, and the conditional status of the CG1 exit criterion against the open §10 storage decision also need tightening before implementation.

criteria: Assess issue 338 append-only sample and provenance safety including conflicting constraints, duplicate observations and source ownership.
Assess issue 339 candidate completeness, review decisions, loop termination, bounded work, atomic row/role rewrites and replay. Cite specific plan locations and falsifiable cases.
rubric.name: Cross-document growth plan
